title: Diffusion Epistemic Uncertainty with Asymmetric Learning for Diffusion-Generated Image Detection
research_problem: Addressing how ignoring the differing impacts of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty on reconstruction error can undermine diffusion-generated image detection performance.
usefulness_reason: Directly tackles diffusion-based measurement limitations by decomposing uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components to improve detection generalizability.
key_findings: Aleatoric uncertainty creates data noise ambiguity and does not help distinguish generated images, whereas epistemic uncertainty supports detection.
The proposed Diffusion Epistemic Uncertainty with Asymmetric Learning (DEUA) framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on large-scale benchmarks.
